Anthropic released the Claude 4 family, consisting of two models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. This dual-model strategy positioned Opus 4 as the flagship model with pricing at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens, while positioning Sonnet 4 as a "fast workhorse" priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens to serve as the developer-default coding model [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled that agentic coding had become a defining market trend in 2025, driven specifically by the rise of the Claude Code product [Source: ev-1]. By introducing "computer use 2.0," which was roughly twice as reliable as the previous 3.x generation, Anthropic positioned itself against competitors like OpenAI's o-series during an enterprise agentic-coding gold rush [Source: ev-1]. The company aimed to establish Claude 4 as the safest and most reliable coding agent, a strategy that contributed to record API usage and culminated in a large funding round in late September 2025 at a reported valuation of approximately $183 billion [Source: ev-1].
